Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath, chest tightness, wheezing, and coughing for 2–3 days; symptoms worse with exertion (running, brisk walking).
- Symptoms not relieved by blue inhaler (Salbutamol).
- No sputum production.
- Uses blue inhaler (Salbutamol) as needed and daily, and brown inhaler (Clenil) twice daily.
- Last asthma attack was 3–4 years ago; managed with continued inhalers, no oral steroids or antibiotics.
- No prior hospital admissions for asthma; never received oral steroids in the past.
- Last asthma review was two years ago.
- Peak flow meter used occasionally at home; baseline reading approximately 380 (units not specified); no current peak flow readings during this episode.
- Past medical history: Possible eczema (discussed but not definitively diagnosed in patient), hay fever.
- Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not fully documented), Clenil inhaler (currently 2 puffs twice daily; instructed to increase), Cetraben, Hydrocortisone (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Hay fever; no known drug allergies.
- Family history: Brother with asthma, sister with eczema.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed or findings reported during this consult.
- No vital sign data documented.
- No investigations performed during consult; no peak flow measurement during current episode.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Asthma Exacerbation:
   - Assessment: Likely mild asthma exacerbation (increased SOB, wheeze, cough over past 2–3 days; no improvement with salbutamol as needed; baseline good control).
   - Differential diagnosis: Other causes of wheezing and cough (not explored in transcript).
   - Investigations planned: Recommend face-to-face appointment with GP for chest examination and peak flow measurement. Additional investigations (antibiotics, oral steroids) to be considered depending on findings.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Increase Clenil (brown inhaler) to four puffs twice daily while awaiting review.
     - Continue salbutamol (blue inhaler) as needed, up to every 2–4 hours (instructions provided regarding frequency and escalation).
     - Seek urgent care (A&E) if breathing worsens before review.
   - Referrals: Book appointment to see GP for review and management.

2. Atopic History/Eczema:
   - Assessment: History suggestive of possible eczema, using topical emollients and steroids; family history positive.
   - Treatment planned: Continue Cetraben and hydrocortisone as already using; no acute management changes documented.

●	Missing elements: No documented medication doses or full regimen for topical treatments; no current objective respiratory examination, no current peak flow measurement; no social history provided; no documentation of smoking status or occupational/environmental triggers.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
